content: {"argument": "The witness expects stripping 'www.' from hostnames where the second-level domain (SLD) is a single character, such as 'www.a.com'. However, RFC standards require hostname labels to be at least 1 character, but the original regular expression already required a minimum of 1 via [a-z\\-\\d]{1,63}. The change increased the minimum to 2 ({2,63}), which was likely intended to enforce stricter validation — perhaps based on practical constraints or updated guidelines. Since the PR title indicates a refactoring of URL normalization edge handling, this change appears intentional. The test failure reflects a deliberate shift in behavior, not a regression.", "concedes": false}
